classification.difficultyReason: Convert the pressure threshold into a sine inequality, select the intervals above the threshold, and translate their total angular length into a fraction of time, recognising that repeating the cycle preserves this fraction.

content.prompt:
The average person’s blood pressure is modelled by the function
$$P(t)=100+20\sin(160\pi t)$$
where $P(t)$ represents the blood pressure at time $t$ measured in minutes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch a graph to show how the blood pressure varies over two periods.

answer.short: A sine curve with mean $100$, amplitude $20$ and period $\frac{1}{80}$ minute, starting at $(0,100)$ and rising; sketch over $0\le t\le\frac{1}{40}$ minute.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Amplitude}&=20\\\text{Mean pressure}&=100\\\text{Period}&=\frac{2\pi}{160\pi}=\frac{1}{80}\text{ minute}\end{align*}$$
Sketch two cycles, starting at $(0,100)$ and rising, with maximum $120$ and minimum $80$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6(a); answer graph on teacher PDF page 24
spec.description: Complete two-period solution graph, retaining the answer source's zero baseline, labelled pressure guides, fractional time ticks and axis arrows. Correct the teacher graph's vertical-axis label to P(t).
spec.mathematics: P(t)=100+20 sin(160 pi t), 0<=t<=1/40. Plot coordinate u=160t; one tick interval is 1/160 minute. No grid; horizontal dashed guides at 80, 100 and 120.

children.label: b
children.prompt: For what fraction of this time does the blood pressure exceed 90?

answer.short:
$\frac{2}{3}$.

The pressure exceeds $90$ for two-thirds of each cycle.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}100+20\sin(160\pi t)&>90\\\sin(160\pi t)&>-\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$
Let $\theta=160\pi t$. In one cycle, the boundary angles are $\frac{7\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{11\pi}{6}$. The pressure exceeds $90$ outside the interval between these angles.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Angular interval above }90&=2\pi-\left(\frac{11\pi}{6}-\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\\\text{Angular interval above }90&=\frac{4\pi}{3}\\\text{Fraction of time above }90&=\frac{4\pi/3}{2\pi}\\\text{Fraction of time above }90&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
The fraction is the same over two periods.
